figures.finding: Palau's National Code (21 PNC § 105, "Age of majority") makes everyone residing in the Republic who has attained eighteen of legal age.

sources.said: All persons, whether male or female, residing in the Republic, who shall have attained the age of 18 years shall be regarded as of legal age and their period of minority to have ceased.

figures.finding: Palau reported that only two labour laws mention children: none under sixteen on Republic vessels in foreign trade (save family vessels, school- and training ships), and no one under twenty-one where alcohol is served; so there is no general minimum working age, and nothing reaches a child performer.

sources.said: Only two labour laws specifically make reference to children:
Children under the age of 16 years shall not be employed on Republic vessels engaged in foreign trade
A licensee shall not employ any person under the age of 21 years in or about that portion of the premises which is used for the serving and consumption of alcoholic beverages.

sources.title: Palau: second periodic report, CRC/C/PLW/2 (2016, issued 15 March 2017); quotes the Palau National Code, Title 21, § 105
sources.said: All persons, whether male or female, residing in the Republic, who shall have attained the age of 18 years shall be regarded as of legal age and their period of minority to have ceased. … Only two labour laws specifically make reference to children: … Children under the age of 16 years shall not be employed on Republic vessels engaged in foreign trade … A licensee shall not employ any person under the age of 21 years in or about that portion of the premises which is used for the serving and consumption of alcoholic beverages.
